desc:
Start with an array sorted in non-decreasing order (equal values are allowed). Repeat this step some number of times: remove the last element and insert it at the front. The result is nums.

Return the smallest number of steps k ≥ 0 that turns some sorted array into nums. For example [3, 3, 4, 1, 1] comes from [1, 1, 3, 3, 4] after 3 steps, so the answer is 3. An array that is already sorted (including one whose values are all equal) has answer 0.
constraints: nums is a non-decreasing array after some number of the described steps
hints: Without duplicates the answer is the index of the minimum. With duplicates the minimum value can appear many times; which of its positions counts?
The sorted order starts at the one index whose predecessor is larger than it (index 0 if no such index exists). Equal neighbours never mark the start.

Run the 'compare with nums[hi]' search. When nums[mid] == nums[hi] you cannot tell which side holds the start. If nums[hi - 1] > nums[hi] then hi itself is the start, otherwise discard hi with hi -= 1.
editorial: Since the array is a rotation of a sorted one, at most one position i has nums[i - 1] > nums[i]. If there is none the array is sorted and the answer is 0; otherwise the sorted order begins at that i and the answer is exactly i. Duplicates matter only because they make it impossible to decide in O(1) which half to drop.

Keep a window [lo, hi] containing the start. If nums[mid] > nums[hi], the descent is right of mid: lo = mid + 1. If nums[mid] < nums[hi], the descent is at or left of mid: hi = mid. On a tie, first check whether hi is itself the start (nums[hi - 1] > nums[hi]) and return it; if not, hi is not needed and can be dropped, because its left neighbour carries the same or a smaller value. Dropping the minimum value blindly would give a wrong index for arrays like [1, 1, 2, 1], whose answer is 3.

The tie case removes only one element, so the worst case (for example almost all values equal) is O(n); typical inputs finish in O(log n). No algorithm can beat O(n) in the worst case because the single descent could hide anywhere among equal values. Space is O(1).
